verdict: Circle grew revenue 7% to $701M as USDC in circulation rose 19% to $73.3B, and it made a $48M profit — a year earlier, a huge IPO stock-pay bill had driven a $482M loss.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue and reserve income was $701M, up from $658M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs −$4.48 a year ago; net income was $48M

kpis.label: USDC in circulation
kpis.note: End of period, up 19% YoY; the average for the quarter was $76.5B, up 25%

segments.name: Reserve income
segments.note: Interest earned on the cash and U.S. Treasuries backing USDC (a dollar-tracking crypto token). Average USDC in circulation grew 25%, but the return rate on reserves fell 66 basis points to 3.5%, so income grew only 5%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Transaction, subscription and services revenue — up 41% on growth in subscription and services.

opex.name: Compensation expenses
opex.note: Pay and benefits for staff, including stock-based compensation.

opex.name: General and administrative expenses
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal, finance and admin.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization expenses
opex.note: Spreading the cost of software, equipment and acquired assets over their useful lives.

opex.name: IT infrastructure costs
opex.note: The computing and systems that run the platform.

opex.name: Digital assets losses (gains)
opex.note: A $0.7M gain — digital assets held in day-to-day operations rose in value, so this line reduced expenses.

takeaways.title: USDC kept growing
takeaways.text: USDC in circulation ended the quarter at $73.3B, up 19% YoY, and onchain transaction volume hit $14.8 trillion — the network is expanding even as crypto markets cooled.

takeaways.title: Falling rates bite
takeaways.text: The return Circle earns on USDC reserves fell 66 basis points to 3.5%. Balances grew fast enough to offset it this quarter, but reserve income — 95% of all revenue — rises and falls with interest rates.

takeaways.title: Back in profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $48M versus a $482M loss a year ago. The difference is mostly stock pay: $54M this quarter versus $435M in Q2 2025, when the IPO made years of awards vest at once.

oneTimers: Operating expenses include a $5M charitable donation of shares to the Circle Foundation and $10M of one-off legal expenses — items Circle excludes from its non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of $143M.
The year-ago comparison is distorted by the June 2025 IPO: Q2 2025 operating expenses included $435M of stock-based compensation, versus $54M this quarter.
otherDetail: Other income of $17.9M, net: $14.5M of interest on corporate cash, $3.7M of gains on digital assets and strategic investments and $1.5M of currency gains, partly offset by a $1.9M fair-value loss on convertible debt, warrants and derivatives and a $0.1M impairment.
footerNote: Circle's cost of revenue is mostly the cut of reserve income paid to USDC distribution partners like Coinbase.
